sahara-marrakech-3-days:
The road south is part of the pleasure: the folds of the High Atlas, the warm earth of Aït Ben Haddou and the tall walls of Todra Gorge. By the second evening, the landscape opens into dunes and the pace finally slows.

Spend a night near Erg Chebbi before the long road back to Marrakech. This is a full three days, with plenty of time on the road. If you can spare two more, our slower Sahara route gives you a whole day to enjoy the desert.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days:
Begin among the streets and monuments of Morocco’s imperial cities, where a doorway or a small workshop can be as absorbing as a famous landmark. A full day in Fes leaves time to follow those details with a local guide.

Then travel south through mountain country and the Ziz Valley for an evening in the Sahara. Kasbahs and the High Atlas lead you on to Marrakech, with another full day to explore before you leave.
slow-sahara-5-days:
The first evening in the desert is only the beginning. With two nights near Erg Chebbi, there’s time to visit Khamlia, explore the surrounding settlements or simply watch the light move across the sand.

The journey home follows the Draa Valley, with a night near Ouarzazate before the Atlas crossing. Choose a camp, a lodge or a night in each—the right combination depends on how you like to spend your evenings.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days:
Leave Marrakech across the Atlas and spend the first night in Dades. Beyond Todra Gorge, the road leads toward Merzouga and the broad sands of Erg Chebbi.

Two nights in the desert region leave a day for Khamlia, nearby settlements and quiet time at the dunes. Then follow the Ziz Valley and Middle Atlas north to Fes, arriving somewhere entirely different from where you began.
southern-morocco-7-days:
An evening near Aït Ben Haddou, palms around Skoura, the changing shapes of the Dades Valley: this journey gives the approach to the Sahara its own time and attention.

Near Merzouga, two nights make space for village visits, dune walks and a quieter afternoon. The return is broken near Ouarzazate, so the final Atlas crossing has a day of its own.
coast-desert-8-days:
Travel through the Atlas and Todra Gorge to a Sahara overnight, then turn west through Ouarzazate and Taroudant. By Essaouira, mountain roads have given way to sea air and fishing boats.

Two nights on the coast leave a full day for the medina, ramparts and a long lunch near the port. There’s a good deal of ground to cover between these landscapes; the reward is seeing how different one part of Morocco feels from the next.
north-sahara-10-days:
Begin beside the Strait in Tangier before spending a night among Chefchaouen’s blue lanes. In Fes, a day with a local guide brings you closer to the workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods within the medina.

The route then turns south through the Ziz Valley to Merzouga. A desert day, Todra Gorge and the High Atlas lead you onward to Marrakech, without doubling back to your starting point.
grand-morocco-14-days:
There’s time here to see the country change: from Rabat and Chefchaouen to Fes, then through the mountains toward the Sahara. Full days in several stops let you do more than arrive, look around and leave.

After the desert and southern valleys, Marrakech brings gardens and lively souks. The journey finishes with Essaouira’s sea air before the return to Marrakech. It’s a wide-ranging first visit, with room to add a night wherever you’d like to linger.
ouzoud-waterfalls:
The sound of the falls reaches you before the view opens. Paths weave between fig and olive trees, revealing different angles on the cascades as you make your way into the gorge.

With four to five hours in the area, there’s time for the walk, a riverside lunch and an optional boat ride near the spray. Your driver-guide stays with your group, with a walking pace that leaves room to stop and enjoy the surroundings.
ourika-valley:
As the road follows the river into the Atlas foothills, Marrakech begins to feel a world away. Terraced fields and villages line the valley, and the cafés at Setti Fatma invite you to stay for lunch.

Walk up to the first waterfall if you’d like a more active day, or keep to the village and riverbank. Either way, there’s time to enjoy the scenery without hurrying from one stop to the next.
essaouira-day:
Essaouira feels different from the moment you arrive: cooler air, gulls over the harbor and the Atlantic just beyond the medina walls. Walk between small workshops and galleries, then follow the boats to the fishing port.

The afternoon is yours to enjoy. Find a table for lunch, browse the souks or pause for mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Your driver takes care of the return to Marrakech; if a single day feels too short, ask us about staying overnight.
ait-ben-haddou-day:
The Atlas crossing offers a changing view at every turn: hillside villages, cultivated terraces and peaks rising above the road. Beyond the pass, Aït Ben Haddou stands in warm earth against the valley.

Explore its lanes and climb toward the old granary before continuing to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. Film lovers can add a visit to the Atlas studios. It’s a long day, but a striking introduction to the landscapes south of Marrakech.
agafay-evening:
Beyond Marrakech, the stone desert opens into low hills and a wide horizon. Arrive with time to take in the late-afternoon light before dinner at your chosen venue.

You can keep the evening simple—a view, a meal and time together—or add a camel ride or quad outing. We’ll help you choose the setting and agree the details before you go.
imlil-atlas-day:
See the landscapes around Marrakech change in a single day: Agafay’s stony hills, the water at Lalla Takerkoust and the terraces below the Kik Plateau. A camel ride and tea with a Berber family bring time to pause between the views.

In Imlil, leave the road for a walk with a mountain guide. Paths lead past walnut trees, hamlets and streams before lunch in a Berber home. The return follows Moulay Brahim Gorge back toward Marrakech.
chefchaouen-from-fes:
The road from Fes leads north toward the Rif and the hillside town of Chefchaouen. Once there, narrow blue lanes and small squares invite a slower kind of exploring.

Spend the middle of the day on foot, pausing for lunch and photographs before the return. If you’d like to enjoy the town after the day visitors leave, we can discuss an overnight stay instead.
volubilis-meknes:
Begin among the open-air remains of Volubilis, where walking through the site gives a sense of the city that once stood here. Nearby Moulay Idriss brings a different setting, with a short visit and time for lunch.

Continue to Meknes for the afternoon before returning to Fes. The day’s monument visits follow current access arrangements, leaving room to enjoy the places that are open.
marrakech-balloon:
An early start brings you to the launch area while the day is still beginning. After the briefing and preparations, take to the sky when conditions allow and watch the countryside spread out below.

The flight is one part of the morning, with breakfast and transfers arranged according to your chosen session. Leave the rest of the morning open so there’s no need to rush after landing.
agafay-quad:
Agafay’s terrain gives this outing its character: stony tracks, low hills and long views. A briefing and practice session at the base help you settle in before the ride begins.

Follow your guide along the agreed route, pausing to take in the scenery. We’ll make the time on the trail, transfers and driver or passenger arrangements clear when planning your outing.
merzouga-camel:
A camel’s measured pace gives you time to look around: the shape of the dunes, the changing light and the space beyond the next ridge. Follow a short route from Merzouga before returning to your starting point.

Choose the time that suits your stay and comfort. A 4×4 alternative can be discussed if camel riding isn’t for you, and a camp night can be arranged separately.
merzouga-sandboarding:
Add a little play to a desert stay. Start on a suitable dune, learn the basics and find your own rhythm, with time to rest between the climbs back up.

The session is planned around the heat and wind. It works well as a local activity while staying in Merzouga; transfers and overnight camp stays are separate arrangements.
agafay-buggy:
Meet at the base, learn the controls and settle into your seat before following the guide into Agafay’s open landscape. Scenic pauses give you time to look beyond the trail.

The route responds to conditions on the day. We’ll clarify who’s driving, who’s joining as a passenger and how much time you’ll spend on the trail, alongside the transfers and preparation.
atlas-paragliding:
From the launch site, the landscape takes on a different scale. Meet your pilot, prepare together and take off only when the weather and site conditions are suitable.

Keep your schedule flexible for this outing. The launch location and flight time depend on conditions, and we’ll clarify the operator’s arrangements, eligibility and weather policy before booking.
marrakech-hammam:
After hours on your feet in the medina, a hammam offers a different way to spend part of the day. Warmth, water and a slower pace make the visit as much about taking time as the treatment itself.

A neighborhood bathhouse and a spa are different experiences. We’ll discuss the setting, privacy and treatments with you, so you know what to expect and can choose what feels comfortable.
marrakech-cooking:
There’s something satisfying about learning a dish in the place it comes from. Work through a Moroccan menu with your host, ask questions as you cook and pick up ideas to bring home.

Some classes begin with a market visit; others take you straight to the kitchen. The session ends around the table, enjoying the food together. We’ll agree the menu and dietary needs before you arrive.
marrakech-dinner-show:
Make an evening of it, with dinner and a performance in one setting. The atmosphere, menu and style of show vary by venue, so choosing the right one is part of the planning.

We’ll help clarify the program, drinks and transport before you decide. If you’re traveling with children or prefer an earlier finish, let us know so the evening works for everyone.
essaouira-horse-riding:
A ride outside Essaouira offers a different view of the coast, away from the harbor and busy streets. Begin at the stable, where the team will discuss your experience and introduce you to your horse.

The route and pace suit the riders and conditions. Beach access is not always possible, and a gallop is not part of every ride—the pleasure is in exploring the landscape on horseback.
